# A Topic is generated by a model, then verified against a real search

Stage 2 must show the student 5 to 8 Topics inside the Domain they picked. Fynd asks a model for the Topics, and then searches Semantic Scholar for the Topic the student picked. Fynd keeps the Topic only if the search returns 5 or more Papers with an open copy. A Topic that fails the check goes back to the student with the count shown.

Fynd stores no corpus of its own. Semantic Scholar is the index, and a Topic is a label for a search and not a Claim, so a Topic does not need the citation guard that protects the handover.

## Consequences

The contract is the part that must not change: a Topic reaches the student only if a real search returns enough open Papers for it. The generator behind that contract can change later. A grounded generator, which runs one broad search for the Domain, clusters the titles it gets back, and names each cluster, fits behind the same contract with no change downstream.

A Topic carries two fields. A label the student reads, and a query Fynd searches with. The model returns both in the same structured output, so no later Stage rewrites a label into a query.

The threshold of 5 counts Papers with an open copy, not raw search hits. The PRD allows open abstracts and open full text only, so a paywalled Paper never reaches stage 5. The threshold is one named constant, and it gets tuned when the Seeded Topic shows how many open Papers survive to the Gap.

A Topic is a value on one Project and not a row in a shared table. Two model runs word the same Topic two different ways, so a shared table would need matching logic that buys nothing. The disk cache covers the repeated fetch cost instead.

## Considered options

A curated Topic list for each Domain. Rejected because a closed list needs a human to grow it, and the PRD already asks the model for 5 to 8 Topics.

A corpus Fynd owns, built by reading the papers in a Domain and storing them. Rejected because it is a data engineering project with no payoff, and a search API already holds that index.

A model with no verification. Rejected because the student only finds out at stage 4 that the Topic has no literature, and that is the failure Stage 2 exists to catch.

A count check on all 5 to 8 proposed Topics, before the student picks. Rejected because Semantic Scholar allows 1 request per second, so eight calls make a dropdown slow, and seven of the counts are thrown away.
